common_requirement_context.benchmark/baseline.md:
# External baseline contract (before B01)

The interface is a subprocess CLI run from an isolated working directory.
Commands print exactly one JSON value to stdout on success (exit 0); expected
application failures print `{"error":"CODE"}` to stderr (exit 1). Commands
persist across separate processes in `tasks.json` in that directory. `list`
on missing storage returns `[]` without creating the file.

Each task result has exactly `id`, `title`, `description`, `status`, `priority`,
`created_at`, and `due_date`. IDs are unique nonempty strings; timestamps are
UTC ISO strings ending in `Z`. Lists sort by `(created_at, id)` ascending.

* `create --title T --description D [--priority LOW|NORMAL|HIGH]
  [--due-date UTC_TIMESTAMP]`: nonblank title, verbatim description, new ID,
  status `pending`, priority default `NORMAL`, current creation timestamp,
  due date default `null`. Blank title fails `invalid_title`; malformed or
  non-UTC due date fails `invalid_due_date` without changing storage.
* `list`: return all tasks including completed tasks.
* `list-high`: return only HIGH tasks (including completed ones).
* `list-overdue`: return only pending tasks with a non-null due date **strictly
  earlier** than current UTC time. Undated and completed tasks are excluded.
* `complete --id ID`: pending task becomes completed and is persisted; a
  missing ID fails `task_not_found`, an already completed task fails
  `invalid_transition`, both without altering the stored file.
* `delete --id ID`: remove and return the task (pending or completed); missing
  ID fails `task_not_found` without altering storage.
* `migrate`: explicit conversion of legacy unversioned records to version 3
  (add `priority: NORMAL`, `due_date: null`) and version 2 records to version 3
  (add `due_date: null`); return `{"migrated": N}`. Running on current data or
  absent storage returns `{"migrated": 0}`. Legacy reads fail
  `migration_required` without changing data. New writes use a version-3
  envelope with `schema_version` and `records`.

Malformed JSON and invalid record shape, duplicate IDs, blank IDs/titles,
invalid enums and timestamps fail `invalid_state` on read. Failed operations
must not mutate persisted bytes. An exact-time overdue boundary can be checked
only with a controlled clock; the external CLI oracle checks widely separated
past and future instants instead of relying on timing-sensitive sleeps.

The oracle exercises *both* executable CLIs with fresh subprocesses and
independent temporary directories; it asserts this contract before comparing
normalized outcomes. Random IDs and wall-clock timestamps are checked for
properties, not falsely required to be byte-identical across tracks.
common_requirement_context.benchmark/requirements/README.md:
# Frozen sequential change set

Execute B01–B20 in numeric order; a change is cumulative. Each file states an
observable API and acceptance criteria, not an implementation strategy. New
fields on existing tasks require an explicit `migrate` path; ordinary reads of
old storage must report `migration_required` without mutation. Migration is
atomic, returns the number of migrated tasks, and is idempotent. Missing IDs
return `task_not_found` unless a request explicitly defines another error.
Successful operations output JSON; application errors use the baseline JSON
error envelope and exit 1. New list commands use the baseline `(created_at,
id)` sort unless stated otherwise. Existing commands remain compatible unless
a request expressly changes them. Errors must leave observable state intact.

IDs and test cases are fixed before execution; correcting a faulty requirement
requires a recorded protocol deviation, never a silent retroactive edit.
The authoritative frozen file hashes are in `../results/BASELINE.md`.

# External baseline contract (before B01)

The interface is a subprocess CLI run from an isolated working directory.
Commands print exactly one JSON value to stdout on success (exit 0); expected
application failures print `{"error":"CODE"}` to stderr (exit 1). Commands
persist across separate processes in `tasks.json` in that directory. `list`
on missing storage returns `[]` without creating the file.

Each task result has exactly `id`, `title`, `description`, `status`, `priority`,
`created_at`, and `due_date`. IDs are unique nonempty strings; timestamps are
UTC ISO strings ending in `Z`. Lists sort by `(created_at, id)` ascending.

* `create --title T --description D [--priority LOW|NORMAL|HIGH]
  [--due-date UTC_TIMESTAMP]`: nonblank title, verbatim description, new ID,
  status `pending`, priority default `NORMAL`, current creation timestamp,
  due date default `null`. Blank title fails `invalid_title`; malformed or
  non-UTC due date fails `invalid_due_date` without changing storage.
* `list`: return all tasks including completed tasks.
* `list-high`: return only HIGH tasks (including completed ones).
* `list-overdue`: return only pending tasks with a non-null due date **strictly
  earlier** than current UTC time. Undated and completed tasks are excluded.
* `complete --id ID`: pending task becomes completed and is persisted; a
  missing ID fails `task_not_found`, an already completed task fails
  `invalid_transition`, both without altering the stored file.
* `delete --id ID`: remove and return the task (pending or completed); missing
  ID fails `task_not_found` without altering storage.
* `migrate`: explicit conversion of legacy unversioned records to version 3
  (add `priority: NORMAL`, `due_date: null`) and version 2 records to version 3
  (add `due_date: null`); return `{"migrated": N}`. Running on current data or
  absent storage returns `{"migrated": 0}`. Legacy reads fail
  `migration_required` without changing data. New writes use a version-3
  envelope with `schema_version` and `records`.

Malformed JSON and invalid record shape, duplicate IDs, blank IDs/titles,
invalid enums and timestamps fail `invalid_state` on read. Failed operations
must not mutate persisted bytes. An exact-time overdue boundary can be checked
only with a controlled clock; the external CLI oracle checks widely separated
past and future instants instead of relying on timing-sensitive sleeps.

independent temporary directories; it asserts this contract before comparing
normalized outcomes. Random IDs and wall-clock timestamps are checked for
properties, not falsely required to be byte-identical across tracks.

common_requirement_context.benchmark/baseline.md:
# External baseline contract (before B01)

The interface is a subprocess CLI run from an isolated working directory.
Commands print exactly one JSON value to stdout on success (exit 0); expected
application failures print `{"error":"CODE"}` to stderr (exit 1). Commands
persist across separate processes in `tasks.json` in that directory. `list`
on missing storage returns `[]` without creating the file.

Each task result has exactly `id`, `title`, `description`, `status`, `priority`,
`created_at`, and `due_date`. IDs are unique nonempty strings; timestamps are
UTC ISO strings ending in `Z`. Lists sort by `(created_at, id)` ascending.

* `create --title T --description D [--priority LOW|NORMAL|HIGH]
  [--due-date UTC_TIMESTAMP]`: nonblank title, verbatim description, new ID,
  status `pending`, priority default `NORMAL`, current creation timestamp,
  due date default `null`. Blank title fails `invalid_title`; malformed or
  non-UTC due date fails `invalid_due_date` without changing storage.
* `list`: return all tasks including completed tasks.
* `list-high`: return only HIGH tasks (including completed ones).
* `list-overdue`: return only pending tasks with a non-null due date **strictly
  earlier** than current UTC time. Undated and completed tasks are excluded.
* `complete --id ID`: pending task becomes completed and is persisted; a
  missing ID fails `task_not_found`, an already completed task fails
  `invalid_transition`, both without altering the stored file.
* `delete --id ID`: remove and return the task (pending or completed); missing
  ID fails `task_not_found` without altering storage.
* `migrate`: explicit conversion of legacy unversioned records to version 3
  (add `priority: NORMAL`, `due_date: null`) and version 2 records to version 3
  (add `due_date: null`); return `{"migrated": N}`. Running on current data or
  absent storage returns `{"migrated": 0}`. Legacy reads fail
  `migration_required` without changing data. New writes use a version-3
  envelope with `schema_version` and `records`.

Malformed JSON and invalid record shape, duplicate IDs, blank IDs/titles,
invalid enums and timestamps fail `invalid_state` on read. Failed operations
must not mutate persisted bytes. An exact-time overdue boundary can be checked
only with a controlled clock; the external CLI oracle checks widely separated
past and future instants instead of relying on timing-sensitive sleeps.

The oracle exercises *both* executable CLIs with fresh subprocesses and
independent temporary directories; it asserts this contract before comparing
normalized outcomes. Random IDs and wall-clock timestamps are checked for
properties, not falsely required to be byte-identical across tracks.
common_requirement_context.benchmark/requirements/README.md:
# Frozen sequential change set

Execute B01–B20 in numeric order; a change is cumulative. Each file states an
observable API and acceptance criteria, not an implementation strategy. New
fields on existing tasks require an explicit `migrate` path; ordinary reads of
old storage must report `migration_required` without mutation. Migration is
atomic, returns the number of migrated tasks, and is idempotent. Missing IDs
return `task_not_found` unless a request explicitly defines another error.
Successful operations output JSON; application errors use the baseline JSON
error envelope and exit 1. New list commands use the baseline `(created_at,
id)` sort unless stated otherwise. Existing commands remain compatible unless
a request expressly changes them. Errors must leave observable state intact.

IDs and test cases are fixed before execution; correcting a faulty requirement
requires a recorded protocol deviation, never a silent retroactive edit.
The authoritative frozen file hashes are in `../results/BASELINE.md`.

`created_at`, and `due_date`. IDs are unique nonempty strings; timestamps are
UTC ISO strings ending in `Z`. Lists sort by `(created_at, id)` ascending.

  status `pending`, priority default `NORMAL`, current creation timestamp,
  due date default `null`. Blank title fails `invalid_title`; malformed or
  non-UTC due date fails `invalid_due_date` without changing storage.
* `list`: return all tasks including completed tasks.
* `list-high`: return only HIGH tasks (including completed ones).
* `list-overdue`: return only pending tasks with a non-null due date **strictly
  earlier** than current UTC time. Undated and completed tasks are excluded.

  missing ID fails `task_not_found`, an already completed task fails
  `invalid_transition`, both without altering the stored file.

  ID fails `task_not_found` without altering storage.

  (add `due_date: null`); return `{"migrated": N}`. Running on current data or
  absent storage returns `{"migrated": 0}`. Legacy reads fail
  `migration_required` without changing data. New writes use a version-3
  envelope with `schema_version` and `records`.

invalid enums and timestamps fail `invalid_state` on read. Failed operations

common_requirement_context.benchmark/baseline.md:
# External baseline contract (before B01)

The interface is a subprocess CLI run from an isolated working directory.
Commands print exactly one JSON value to stdout on success (exit 0); expected
application failures print `{"error":"CODE"}` to stderr (exit 1). Commands
persist across separate processes in `tasks.json` in that directory. `list`
on missing storage returns `[]` without creating the file.

Each task result has exactly `id`, `title`, `description`, `status`, `priority`,
`created_at`, and `due_date`. IDs are unique nonempty strings; timestamps are
UTC ISO strings ending in `Z`. Lists sort by `(created_at, id)` ascending.

* `create --title T --description D [--priority LOW|NORMAL|HIGH]
  [--due-date UTC_TIMESTAMP]`: nonblank title, verbatim description, new ID,
  status `pending`, priority default `NORMAL`, current creation timestamp,
  due date default `null`. Blank title fails `invalid_title`; malformed or
  non-UTC due date fails `invalid_due_date` without changing storage.
* `list`: return all tasks including completed tasks.
* `list-high`: return only HIGH tasks (including completed ones).
* `list-overdue`: return only pending tasks with a non-null due date **strictly
  earlier** than current UTC time. Undated and completed tasks are excluded.
* `complete --id ID`: pending task becomes completed and is persisted; a
  missing ID fails `task_not_found`, an already completed task fails
  `invalid_transition`, both without altering the stored file.
* `delete --id ID`: remove and return the task (pending or completed); missing
  ID fails `task_not_found` without altering storage.
* `migrate`: explicit conversion of legacy unversioned records to version 3
  (add `priority: NORMAL`, `due_date: null`) and version 2 records to version 3
  (add `due_date: null`); return `{"migrated": N}`. Running on current data or
  absent storage returns `{"migrated": 0}`. Legacy reads fail
  `migration_required` without changing data. New writes use a version-3
  envelope with `schema_version` and `records`.

Malformed JSON and invalid record shape, duplicate IDs, blank IDs/titles,
invalid enums and timestamps fail `invalid_state` on read. Failed operations
must not mutate persisted bytes. An exact-time overdue boundary can be checked
only with a controlled clock; the external CLI oracle checks widely separated
past and future instants instead of relying on timing-sensitive sleeps.

The oracle exercises *both* executable CLIs with fresh subprocesses and
independent temporary directories; it asserts this contract before comparing
normalized outcomes. Random IDs and wall-clock timestamps are checked for
properties, not falsely required to be byte-identical across tracks.

common_requirement_context.benchmark/baseline.md:
# External baseline contract (before B01)

The interface is a subprocess CLI run from an isolated working directory.
Commands print exactly one JSON value to stdout on success (exit 0); expected
application failures print `{"error":"CODE"}` to stderr (exit 1). Commands
persist across separate processes in `tasks.json` in that directory. `list`
on missing storage returns `[]` without creating the file.

Each task result has exactly `id`, `title`, `description`, `status`, `priority`,
`created_at`, and `due_date`. IDs are unique nonempty strings; timestamps are
UTC ISO strings ending in `Z`. Lists sort by `(created_at, id)` ascending.

* `create --title T --description D [--priority LOW|NORMAL|HIGH]
  [--due-date UTC_TIMESTAMP]`: nonblank title, verbatim description, new ID,
  status `pending`, priority default `NORMAL`, current creation timestamp,
  due date default `null`. Blank title fails `invalid_title`; malformed or
  non-UTC due date fails `invalid_due_date` without changing storage.
* `list`: return all tasks including completed tasks.
* `list-high`: return only HIGH tasks (including completed ones).
* `list-overdue`: return only pending tasks with a non-null due date **strictly
  earlier** than current UTC time. Undated and completed tasks are excluded.
* `complete --id ID`: pending task becomes completed and is persisted; a
  missing ID fails `task_not_found`, an already completed task fails
  `invalid_transition`, both without altering the stored file.
* `delete --id ID`: remove and return the task (pending or completed); missing
  ID fails `task_not_found` without altering storage.
* `migrate`: explicit conversion of legacy unversioned records to version 3
  (add `priority: NORMAL`, `due_date: null`) and version 2 records to version 3
  (add `due_date: null`); return `{"migrated": N}`. Running on current data or
  absent storage returns `{"migrated": 0}`. Legacy reads fail
  `migration_required` without changing data. New writes use a version-3
  envelope with `schema_version` and `records`.

Malformed JSON and invalid record shape, duplicate IDs, blank IDs/titles,
invalid enums and timestamps fail `invalid_state` on read. Failed operations
must not mutate persisted bytes. An exact-time overdue boundary can be checked
only with a controlled clock; the external CLI oracle checks widely separated
past and future instants instead of relying on timing-sensitive sleeps.

The oracle exercises *both* executable CLIs with fresh subprocesses and
independent temporary directories; it asserts this contract before comparing
normalized outcomes. Random IDs and wall-clock timestamps are checked for
properties, not falsely required to be byte-identical across tracks.

# External baseline contract (before B01)

The interface is a subprocess CLI run from an isolated working directory.
Commands print exactly one JSON value to stdout on success (exit 0); expected
application failures print `{"error":"CODE"}` to stderr (exit 1). Commands
persist across separate processes in `tasks.json` in that directory. `list`
on missing storage returns `[]` without creating the file.

Each task result has exactly `id`, `title`, `description`, `status`, `priority`,
`created_at`, and `due_date`. IDs are unique nonempty strings; timestamps are
UTC ISO strings ending in `Z`. Lists sort by `(created_at, id)` ascending.

* `create --title T --description D [--priority LOW|NORMAL|HIGH]
  [--due-date UTC_TIMESTAMP]`: nonblank title, verbatim description, new ID,
  status `pending`, priority default `NORMAL`, current creation timestamp,
  due date default `null`. Blank title fails `invalid_title`; malformed or
  non-UTC due date fails `invalid_due_date` without changing storage.
* `list`: return all tasks including completed tasks.
* `list-high`: return only HIGH tasks (including completed ones).
* `list-overdue`: return only pending tasks with a non-null due date **strictly
  earlier** than current UTC time. Undated and completed tasks are excluded.
* `complete --id ID`: pending task becomes completed and is persisted; a
  missing ID fails `task_not_found`, an already completed task fails
  `invalid_transition`, both without altering the stored file.
* `delete --id ID`: remove and return the task (pending or completed); missing
  ID fails `task_not_found` without altering storage.
* `migrate`: explicit conversion of legacy unversioned records to version 3
  (add `priority: NORMAL`, `due_date: null`) and version 2 records to version 3
  (add `due_date: null`); return `{"migrated": N}`. Running on current data or
  absent storage returns `{"migrated": 0}`. Legacy reads fail
  `migration_required` without changing data. New writes use a version-3
  envelope with `schema_version` and `records`.

Malformed JSON and invalid record shape, duplicate IDs, blank IDs/titles,
invalid enums and timestamps fail `invalid_state` on read. Failed operations
must not mutate persisted bytes. An exact-time overdue boundary can be checked
only with a controlled clock; the external CLI oracle checks widely separated
past and future instants instead of relying on timing-sensitive sleeps.

The oracle exercises *both* executable CLIs with fresh subprocesses and
independent temporary directories; it asserts this contract before comparing
normalized outcomes. Random IDs and wall-clock timestamps are checked for
properties, not falsely required to be byte-identical across tracks.

# External baseline contract (before B01)

The interface is a subprocess CLI run from an isolated working directory.
Commands print exactly one JSON value to stdout on success (exit 0); expected
application failures print `{"error":"CODE"}` to stderr (exit 1). Commands
persist across separate processes in `tasks.json` in that directory. `list`
on missing storage returns `[]` without creating the file.

Each task result has exactly `id`, `title`, `description`, `status`, `priority`,
`created_at`, and `due_date`. IDs are unique nonempty strings; timestamps are
UTC ISO strings ending in `Z`. Lists sort by `(created_at, id)` ascending.

* `create --title T --description D [--priority LOW|NORMAL|HIGH]
  [--due-date UTC_TIMESTAMP]`: nonblank title, verbatim description, new ID,
  status `pending`, priority default `NORMAL`, current creation timestamp,
  due date default `null`. Blank title fails `invalid_title`; malformed or
  non-UTC due date fails `invalid_due_date` without changing storage.
* `list`: return all tasks including completed tasks.
* `list-high`: return only HIGH tasks (including completed ones).
* `list-overdue`: return only pending tasks with a non-null due date **strictly
  earlier** than current UTC time. Undated and completed tasks are excluded.

  missing ID fails `task_not_found`, an already completed task fails
  `invalid_transition`, both without altering the stored file.
* `delete --id ID`: remove and return the task (pending or completed); missing
  ID fails `task_not_found` without altering storage.
* `migrate`: explicit conversion of legacy unversioned records to version 3
  (add `priority: NORMAL`, `due_date: null`) and version 2 records to version 3
  (add `due_date: null`); return `{"migrated": N}`. Running on current data or
  absent storage returns `{"migrated": 0}`. Legacy reads fail
  `migration_required` without changing data. New writes use a version-3
  envelope with `schema_version` and `records`.

Malformed JSON and invalid record shape, duplicate IDs, blank IDs/titles,
invalid enums and timestamps fail `invalid_state` on read. Failed operations
must not mutate persisted bytes. An exact-time overdue boundary can be checked
only with a controlled clock; the external CLI oracle checks widely separated
past and future instants instead of relying on timing-sensitive sleeps.

The oracle exercises *both* executable CLIs with fresh subprocesses and
independent temporary directories; it asserts this contract before comparing
normalized outcomes. Random IDs and wall-clock timestamps are checked for
properties, not falsely required to be byte-identical across tracks.

common_requirement_context.benchmark/baseline.md:
# External baseline contract (before B01)

The interface is a subprocess CLI run from an isolated working directory.
Commands print exactly one JSON value to stdout on success (exit 0); expected
application failures print `{"error":"CODE"}` to stderr (exit 1). Commands
persist across separate processes in `tasks.json` in that directory. `list`
on missing storage returns `[]` without creating the file.

Each task result has exactly `id`, `title`, `description`, `status`, `priority`,
`created_at`, and `due_date`. IDs are unique nonempty strings; timestamps are
UTC ISO strings ending in `Z`. Lists sort by `(created_at, id)` ascending.

* `create --title T --description D [--priority LOW|NORMAL|HIGH]
  [--due-date UTC_TIMESTAMP]`: nonblank title, verbatim description, new ID,
  status `pending`, priority default `NORMAL`, current creation timestamp,
  due date default `null`. Blank title fails `invalid_title`; malformed or
  non-UTC due date fails `invalid_due_date` without changing storage.
* `list`: return all tasks including completed tasks.
* `list-high`: return only HIGH tasks (including completed ones).
* `list-overdue`: return only pending tasks with a non-null due date **strictly
  earlier** than current UTC time. Undated and completed tasks are excluded.
* `complete --id ID`: pending task becomes completed and is persisted; a
  missing ID fails `task_not_found`, an already completed task fails
  `invalid_transition`, both without altering the stored file.
* `delete --id ID`: remove and return the task (pending or completed); missing
  ID fails `task_not_found` without altering storage.
* `migrate`: explicit conversion of legacy unversioned records to version 3
  (add `priority: NORMAL`, `due_date: null`) and version 2 records to version 3
  (add `due_date: null`); return `{"migrated": N}`. Running on current data or
  absent storage returns `{"migrated": 0}`. Legacy reads fail
  `migration_required` without changing data. New writes use a version-3
  envelope with `schema_version` and `records`.

Malformed JSON and invalid record shape, duplicate IDs, blank IDs/titles,
invalid enums and timestamps fail `invalid_state` on read. Failed operations
must not mutate persisted bytes. An exact-time overdue boundary can be checked
only with a controlled clock; the external CLI oracle checks widely separated
past and future instants instead of relying on timing-sensitive sleeps.

The oracle exercises *both* executable CLIs with fresh subprocesses and
independent temporary directories; it asserts this contract before comparing
normalized outcomes. Random IDs and wall-clock timestamps are checked for
properties, not falsely required to be byte-identical across tracks.

common_requirement_context.benchmark/baseline.md:
# External baseline contract (before B01)

The interface is a subprocess CLI run from an isolated working directory.
Commands print exactly one JSON value to stdout on success (exit 0); expected
application failures print `{"error":"CODE"}` to stderr (exit 1). Commands
persist across separate processes in `tasks.json` in that directory. `list`
on missing storage returns `[]` without creating the file.

Each task result has exactly `id`, `title`, `description`, `status`, `priority`,
`created_at`, and `due_date`. IDs are unique nonempty strings; timestamps are
UTC ISO strings ending in `Z`. Lists sort by `(created_at, id)` ascending.

* `create --title T --description D [--priority LOW|NORMAL|HIGH]
  [--due-date UTC_TIMESTAMP]`: nonblank title, verbatim description, new ID,
  status `pending`, priority default `NORMAL`, current creation timestamp,
  due date default `null`. Blank title fails `invalid_title`; malformed or
  non-UTC due date fails `invalid_due_date` without changing storage.
* `list`: return all tasks including completed tasks.
* `list-high`: return only HIGH tasks (including completed ones).
* `list-overdue`: return only pending tasks with a non-null due date **strictly
  earlier** than current UTC time. Undated and completed tasks are excluded.
* `complete --id ID`: pending task becomes completed and is persisted; a
  missing ID fails `task_not_found`, an already completed task fails
  `invalid_transition`, both without altering the stored file.
* `delete --id ID`: remove and return the task (pending or completed); missing
  ID fails `task_not_found` without altering storage.
* `migrate`: explicit conversion of legacy unversioned records to version 3
  (add `priority: NORMAL`, `due_date: null`) and version 2 records to version 3
  (add `due_date: null`); return `{"migrated": N}`. Running on current data or
  absent storage returns `{"migrated": 0}`. Legacy reads fail
  `migration_required` without changing data. New writes use a version-3
  envelope with `schema_version` and `records`.

Malformed JSON and invalid record shape, duplicate IDs, blank IDs/titles,
invalid enums and timestamps fail `invalid_state` on read. Failed operations
must not mutate persisted bytes. An exact-time overdue boundary can be checked
only with a controlled clock; the external CLI oracle checks widely separated
past and future instants instead of relying on timing-sensitive sleeps.

The oracle exercises *both* executable CLIs with fresh subprocesses and
independent temporary directories; it asserts this contract before comparing
normalized outcomes. Random IDs and wall-clock timestamps are checked for
properties, not falsely required to be byte-identical across tracks.

common_requirement_context.benchmark/baseline.md:
# External baseline contract (before B01)

The interface is a subprocess CLI run from an isolated working directory.
Commands print exactly one JSON value to stdout on success (exit 0); expected
application failures print `{"error":"CODE"}` to stderr (exit 1). Commands
persist across separate processes in `tasks.json` in that directory. `list`
on missing storage returns `[]` without creating the file.

Each task result has exactly `id`, `title`, `description`, `status`, `priority`,
`created_at`, and `due_date`. IDs are unique nonempty strings; timestamps are
UTC ISO strings ending in `Z`. Lists sort by `(created_at, id)` ascending.

* `create --title T --description D [--priority LOW|NORMAL|HIGH]
  [--due-date UTC_TIMESTAMP]`: nonblank title, verbatim description, new ID,
  status `pending`, priority default `NORMAL`, current creation timestamp,
  due date default `null`. Blank title fails `invalid_title`; malformed or
  non-UTC due date fails `invalid_due_date` without changing storage.
* `list`: return all tasks including completed tasks.
* `list-high`: return only HIGH tasks (including completed ones).
* `list-overdue`: return only pending tasks with a non-null due date **strictly
  earlier** than current UTC time. Undated and completed tasks are excluded.
* `complete --id ID`: pending task becomes completed and is persisted; a
  missing ID fails `task_not_found`, an already completed task fails
  `invalid_transition`, both without altering the stored file.
* `delete --id ID`: remove and return the task (pending or completed); missing
  ID fails `task_not_found` without altering storage.
* `migrate`: explicit conversion of legacy unversioned records to version 3
  (add `priority: NORMAL`, `due_date: null`) and version 2 records to version 3
  (add `due_date: null`); return `{"migrated": N}`. Running on current data or
  absent storage returns `{"migrated": 0}`. Legacy reads fail
  `migration_required` without changing data. New writes use a version-3
  envelope with `schema_version` and `records`.

Malformed JSON and invalid record shape, duplicate IDs, blank IDs/titles,
invalid enums and timestamps fail `invalid_state` on read. Failed operations
must not mutate persisted bytes. An exact-time overdue boundary can be checked
only with a controlled clock; the external CLI oracle checks widely separated
past and future instants instead of relying on timing-sensitive sleeps.

The oracle exercises *both* executable CLIs with fresh subprocesses and
independent temporary directories; it asserts this contract before comparing
normalized outcomes. Random IDs and wall-clock timestamps are checked for
properties, not falsely required to be byte-identical across tracks.

# External baseline contract (before B01)

The interface is a subprocess CLI run from an isolated working directory.
Commands print exactly one JSON value to stdout on success (exit 0); expected
application failures print `{"error":"CODE"}` to stderr (exit 1). Commands
persist across separate processes in `tasks.json` in that directory. `list`
on missing storage returns `[]` without creating the file.

Each task result has exactly `id`, `title`, `description`, `status`, `priority`,
`created_at`, and `due_date`. IDs are unique nonempty strings; timestamps are
UTC ISO strings ending in `Z`. Lists sort by `(created_at, id)` ascending.

* `create --title T --description D [--priority LOW|NORMAL|HIGH]
  [--due-date UTC_TIMESTAMP]`: nonblank title, verbatim description, new ID,
  status `pending`, priority default `NORMAL`, current creation timestamp,
  due date default `null`. Blank title fails `invalid_title`; malformed or
  non-UTC due date fails `invalid_due_date` without changing storage.
* `list`: return all tasks including completed tasks.
* `list-high`: return only HIGH tasks (including completed ones).
* `list-overdue`: return only pending tasks with a non-null due date **strictly
  earlier** than current UTC time. Undated and completed tasks are excluded.
* `complete --id ID`: pending task becomes completed and is persisted; a
  missing ID fails `task_not_found`, an already completed task fails
  `invalid_transition`, both without altering the stored file.
* `delete --id ID`: remove and return the task (pending or completed); missing
  ID fails `task_not_found` without altering storage.
* `migrate`: explicit conversion of legacy unversioned records to version 3
  (add `priority: NORMAL`, `due_date: null`) and version 2 records to version 3
  (add `due_date: null`); return `{"migrated": N}`. Running on current data or
  absent storage returns `{"migrated": 0}`. Legacy reads fail
  `migration_required` without changing data. New writes use a version-3
  envelope with `schema_version` and `records`.

Malformed JSON and invalid record shape, duplicate IDs, blank IDs/titles,
invalid enums and timestamps fail `invalid_state` on read. Failed operations
must not mutate persisted bytes. An exact-time overdue boundary can be checked
only with a controlled clock; the external CLI oracle checks widely separated
past and future instants instead of relying on timing-sensitive sleeps.

The oracle exercises *both* executable CLIs with fresh subprocesses and
independent temporary directories; it asserts this contract before comparing
normalized outcomes. Random IDs and wall-clock timestamps are checked for
properties, not falsely required to be byte-identical across tracks.
common_requirement_context.benchmark/requirements/README.md:
# Frozen sequential change set

Execute B01–B20 in numeric order; a change is cumulative. Each file states an
observable API and acceptance criteria, not an implementation strategy. New
fields on existing tasks require an explicit `migrate` path; ordinary reads of
old storage must report `migration_required` without mutation. Migration is
atomic, returns the number of migrated tasks, and is idempotent. Missing IDs
return `task_not_found` unless a request explicitly defines another error.
Successful operations output JSON; application errors use the baseline JSON
error envelope and exit 1. New list commands use the baseline `(created_at,
id)` sort unless stated otherwise. Existing commands remain compatible unless
a request expressly changes them. Errors must leave observable state intact.

IDs and test cases are fixed before execution; correcting a faulty requirement
requires a recorded protocol deviation, never a silent retroactive edit.
The authoritative frozen file hashes are in `../results/BASELINE.md`.

# External baseline contract (before B01)

The interface is a subprocess CLI run from an isolated working directory.
Commands print exactly one JSON value to stdout on success (exit 0); expected
application failures print `{"error":"CODE"}` to stderr (exit 1). Commands
persist across separate processes in `tasks.json` in that directory. `list`
on missing storage returns `[]` without creating the file.

Each task result has exactly `id`, `title`, `description`, `status`, `priority`,
`created_at`, and `due_date`. IDs are unique nonempty strings; timestamps are
UTC ISO strings ending in `Z`. Lists sort by `(created_at, id)` ascending.

* `create --title T --description D [--priority LOW|NORMAL|HIGH]
  [--due-date UTC_TIMESTAMP]`: nonblank title, verbatim description, new ID,
  status `pending`, priority default `NORMAL`, current creation timestamp,
  due date default `null`. Blank title fails `invalid_title`; malformed or
  non-UTC due date fails `invalid_due_date` without changing storage.
* `list`: return all tasks including completed tasks.
* `list-high`: return only HIGH tasks (including completed ones).
* `list-overdue`: return only pending tasks with a non-null due date **strictly
  earlier** than current UTC time. Undated and completed tasks are excluded.
* `complete --id ID`: pending task becomes completed and is persisted; a
  missing ID fails `task_not_found`, an already completed task fails
  `invalid_transition`, both without altering the stored file.
* `delete --id ID`: remove and return the task (pending or completed); missing
  ID fails `task_not_found` without altering storage.
* `migrate`: explicit conversion of legacy unversioned records to version 3
  (add `priority: NORMAL`, `due_date: null`) and version 2 records to version 3
  (add `due_date: null`); return `{"migrated": N}`. Running on current data or
  absent storage returns `{"migrated": 0}`. Legacy reads fail
  `migration_required` without changing data. New writes use a version-3
  envelope with `schema_version` and `records`.

Malformed JSON and invalid record shape, duplicate IDs, blank IDs/titles,
invalid enums and timestamps fail `invalid_state` on read. Failed operations
must not mutate persisted bytes. An exact-time overdue boundary can be checked
only with a controlled clock; the external CLI oracle checks widely separated
past and future instants instead of relying on timing-sensitive sleeps.

The oracle exercises *both* executable CLIs with fresh subprocesses and
independent temporary directories; it asserts this contract before comparing
normalized outcomes. Random IDs and wall-clock timestamps are checked for
properties, not falsely required to be byte-identical across tracks.

obligations.source_quote:
# B14 — Dependencies (invariant)

Each task gains an ordered `dependencies` array of task IDs, initially `[]`
(also on migrated tasks). `add-dependency --id ID --depends-on OTHER_ID`
appends OTHER_ID and returns the updated task. Reject self-references with
`invalid_dependency`, nonexistent OTHER_ID with `task_not_found`, duplicates
and cycles with `invalid_dependency`. A failure leaves both tasks unchanged.
Existing dependencies refer to IDs, including archived tasks. Deleting a task
still referenced by another task fails `dependency_in_use` without changes.

obligations.source_quote:
# B16 — Users and required ownership (architectural)

Add users identified by nonblank, case-sensitive IDs. A built-in `system`
user always exists. `create-user --id USER_ID` returns `{"id": USER_ID}`;
duplicate or blank IDs fail `user_exists` or `invalid_user` respectively.
`list-users` returns those objects ordered by ID. Task creation now
requires `--owner USER_ID` naming an existing user; missing or unknown owner
fails `invalid_owner`. Previously unowned tasks migrate to owner `system`;
migration of a task whose nonempty owner ID has no corresponding user fails
`invalid_owner` without changing data. Creating the user and retrying can
resolve it. Existing owner filters continue to work.

common_requirement_context.benchmark/baseline.md:
# External baseline contract (before B01)

The interface is a subprocess CLI run from an isolated working directory.
Commands print exactly one JSON value to stdout on success (exit 0); expected
application failures print `{"error":"CODE"}` to stderr (exit 1). Commands
persist across separate processes in `tasks.json` in that directory. `list`
on missing storage returns `[]` without creating the file.

Each task result has exactly `id`, `title`, `description`, `status`, `priority`,
`created_at`, and `due_date`. IDs are unique nonempty strings; timestamps are
UTC ISO strings ending in `Z`. Lists sort by `(created_at, id)` ascending.

* `create --title T --description D [--priority LOW|NORMAL|HIGH]
  [--due-date UTC_TIMESTAMP]`: nonblank title, verbatim description, new ID,
  status `pending`, priority default `NORMAL`, current creation timestamp,
  due date default `null`. Blank title fails `invalid_title`; malformed or
  non-UTC due date fails `invalid_due_date` without changing storage.
* `list`: return all tasks including completed tasks.
* `list-high`: return only HIGH tasks (including completed ones).
* `list-overdue`: return only pending tasks with a non-null due date **strictly
  earlier** than current UTC time. Undated and completed tasks are excluded.
* `complete --id ID`: pending task becomes completed and is persisted; a
  missing ID fails `task_not_found`, an already completed task fails
  `invalid_transition`, both without altering the stored file.
* `delete --id ID`: remove and return the task (pending or completed); missing
  ID fails `task_not_found` without altering storage.
* `migrate`: explicit conversion of legacy unversioned records to version 3
  (add `priority: NORMAL`, `due_date: null`) and version 2 records to version 3
  (add `due_date: null`); return `{"migrated": N}`. Running on current data or
  absent storage returns `{"migrated": 0}`. Legacy reads fail
  `migration_required` without changing data. New writes use a version-3
  envelope with `schema_version` and `records`.

Malformed JSON and invalid record shape, duplicate IDs, blank IDs/titles,
invalid enums and timestamps fail `invalid_state` on read. Failed operations
must not mutate persisted bytes. An exact-time overdue boundary can be checked
only with a controlled clock; the external CLI oracle checks widely separated
past and future instants instead of relying on timing-sensitive sleeps.

The oracle exercises *both* executable CLIs with fresh subprocesses and
independent temporary directories; it asserts this contract before comparing
normalized outcomes. Random IDs and wall-clock timestamps are checked for
properties, not falsely required to be byte-identical across tracks.
common_requirement_context.benchmark/requirements/README.md:
# Frozen sequential change set

Execute B01–B20 in numeric order; a change is cumulative. Each file states an
observable API and acceptance criteria, not an implementation strategy. New
fields on existing tasks require an explicit `migrate` path; ordinary reads of
old storage must report `migration_required` without mutation. Migration is
atomic, returns the number of migrated tasks, and is idempotent. Missing IDs
return `task_not_found` unless a request explicitly defines another error.
Successful operations output JSON; application errors use the baseline JSON
error envelope and exit 1. New list commands use the baseline `(created_at,
id)` sort unless stated otherwise. Existing commands remain compatible unless
a request expressly changes them. Errors must leave observable state intact.

IDs and test cases are fixed before execution; correcting a faulty requirement
requires a recorded protocol deviation, never a silent retroactive edit.
The authoritative frozen file hashes are in `../results/BASELINE.md`.

Commands print exactly one JSON value to stdout on success (exit 0); expected
application failures print `{"error":"CODE"}` to stderr (exit 1). Commands
persist across separate processes in `tasks.json` in that directory. `list`
on missing storage returns `[]` without creating the file.

Each task result has exactly `id`, `title`, `description`, `status`, `priority`,
`created_at`, and `due_date`. IDs are unique nonempty strings; timestamps are
UTC ISO strings ending in `Z`. Lists sort by `(created_at, id)` ascending.

* `create --title T --description D [--priority LOW|NORMAL|HIGH]
  [--due-date UTC_TIMESTAMP]`: nonblank title, verbatim description, new ID,
  status `pending`, priority default `NORMAL`, current creation timestamp,
  due date default `null`. Blank title fails `invalid_title`; malformed or
  non-UTC due date fails `invalid_due_date` without changing storage.
* `list`: return all tasks including completed tasks.
* `list-high`: return only HIGH tasks (including completed ones).
* `list-overdue`: return only pending tasks with a non-null due date **strictly
  earlier** than current UTC time. Undated and completed tasks are excluded.
* `complete --id ID`: pending task becomes completed and is persisted; a
  missing ID fails `task_not_found`, an already completed task fails
  `invalid_transition`, both without altering the stored file.
* `delete --id ID`: remove and return the task (pending or completed); missing
  ID fails `task_not_found` without altering storage.
* `migrate`: explicit conversion of legacy unversioned records to version 3
  (add `priority: NORMAL`, `due_date: null`) and version 2 records to version 3
  (add `due_date: null`); return `{"migrated": N}`. Running on current data or
  absent storage returns `{"migrated": 0}`. Legacy reads fail
  `migration_required` without changing data. New writes use a version-3
  envelope with `schema_version` and `records`.

Malformed JSON and invalid record shape, duplicate IDs, blank IDs/titles,
invalid enums and timestamps fail `invalid_state` on read. Failed operations
must not mutate persisted bytes. An exact-time overdue boundary can be checked
only with a controlled clock; the external CLI oracle checks widely separated
past and future instants instead of relying on timing-sensitive sleeps.

The oracle exercises *both* executable CLIs with fresh subprocesses and
independent temporary directories; it asserts this contract before comparing
normalized outcomes. Random IDs and wall-clock timestamps are checked for
properties, not falsely required to be byte-identical across tracks.

spans.quote:
# B16 — Users and required ownership (architectural)

Add users identified by nonblank, case-sensitive IDs. A built-in `system`
user always exists. `create-user --id USER_ID` returns `{"id": USER_ID}`;
duplicate or blank IDs fail `user_exists` or `invalid_user` respectively.
`list-users` returns those objects ordered by ID. Task creation now
requires `--owner USER_ID` naming an existing user; missing or unknown owner
fails `invalid_owner`. Previously unowned tasks migrate to owner `system`;
migration of a task whose nonempty owner ID has no corresponding user fails
`invalid_owner` without changing data. Creating the user and retrying can
resolve it. Existing owner filters continue to work.

parameters.meaning: create-user --role ADMIN|USER; all mutating task commands --actor USER_ID

obligations.source_quote:
# B17 — Roles and actor authorization (architectural)

Users have ADMIN or USER role; `system` is ADMIN. `create-user --role ADMIN|USER`
defaults to USER; user results now include `role`, including the built-in
system user. All mutating task commands require `--actor USER_ID`, an
existing user. A USER may create only tasks they own and mutate only their
own tasks; an ADMIN may create or mutate tasks for any owner. Unknown actor
fails `unknown_actor`, missing actor fails `actor_required`, forbidden action
fails `permission_denied`. Reading/listing remains unrestricted. These checks
precede mutations and must preserve state on failure.

# B17 — Roles and actor authorization (architectural)

Users have ADMIN or USER role; `system` is ADMIN. `create-user --role ADMIN|USER`
defaults to USER; user results now include `role`, including the built-in
system user. All mutating task commands require `--actor USER_ID`, an
existing user. A USER may create only tasks they own and mutate only their
own tasks; an ADMIN may create or mutate tasks for any owner. Unknown actor
fails `unknown_actor`, missing actor fails `actor_required`, forbidden action
fails `permission_denied`. Reading/listing remains unrestricted. These checks
precede mutations and must preserve state on failure.

common_requirement_context.benchmark/baseline.md:
# External baseline contract (before B01)

The interface is a subprocess CLI run from an isolated working directory.
Commands print exactly one JSON value to stdout on success (exit 0); expected
application failures print `{"error":"CODE"}` to stderr (exit 1). Commands
persist across separate processes in `tasks.json` in that directory. `list`
on missing storage returns `[]` without creating the file.

Each task result has exactly `id`, `title`, `description`, `status`, `priority`,
`created_at`, and `due_date`. IDs are unique nonempty strings; timestamps are
UTC ISO strings ending in `Z`. Lists sort by `(created_at, id)` ascending.

* `create --title T --description D [--priority LOW|NORMAL|HIGH]
  [--due-date UTC_TIMESTAMP]`: nonblank title, verbatim description, new ID,
  status `pending`, priority default `NORMAL`, current creation timestamp,
  due date default `null`. Blank title fails `invalid_title`; malformed or
  non-UTC due date fails `invalid_due_date` without changing storage.
* `list`: return all tasks including completed tasks.
* `list-high`: return only HIGH tasks (including completed ones).
* `list-overdue`: return only pending tasks with a non-null due date **strictly
  earlier** than current UTC time. Undated and completed tasks are excluded.
* `complete --id ID`: pending task becomes completed and is persisted; a
  missing ID fails `task_not_found`, an already completed task fails
  `invalid_transition`, both without altering the stored file.
* `delete --id ID`: remove and return the task (pending or completed); missing
  ID fails `task_not_found` without altering storage.
* `migrate`: explicit conversion of legacy unversioned records to version 3
  (add `priority: NORMAL`, `due_date: null`) and version 2 records to version 3
  (add `due_date: null`); return `{"migrated": N}`. Running on current data or
  absent storage returns `{"migrated": 0}`. Legacy reads fail
  `migration_required` without changing data. New writes use a version-3
  envelope with `schema_version` and `records`.

Malformed JSON and invalid record shape, duplicate IDs, blank IDs/titles,
invalid enums and timestamps fail `invalid_state` on read. Failed operations
must not mutate persisted bytes. An exact-time overdue boundary can be checked
only with a controlled clock; the external CLI oracle checks widely separated
past and future instants instead of relying on timing-sensitive sleeps.

The oracle exercises *both* executable CLIs with fresh subprocesses and
independent temporary directories; it asserts this contract before comparing
normalized outcomes. Random IDs and wall-clock timestamps are checked for
properties, not falsely required to be byte-identical across tracks.
common_requirement_context.benchmark/requirements/README.md:
# Frozen sequential change set

Execute B01–B20 in numeric order; a change is cumulative. Each file states an
observable API and acceptance criteria, not an implementation strategy. New
fields on existing tasks require an explicit `migrate` path; ordinary reads of
old storage must report `migration_required` without mutation. Migration is
atomic, returns the number of migrated tasks, and is idempotent. Missing IDs
return `task_not_found` unless a request explicitly defines another error.
Successful operations output JSON; application errors use the baseline JSON
error envelope and exit 1. New list commands use the baseline `(created_at,
id)` sort unless stated otherwise. Existing commands remain compatible unless
a request expressly changes them. Errors must leave observable state intact.

IDs and test cases are fixed before execution; correcting a faulty requirement
requires a recorded protocol deviation, never a silent retroactive edit.
The authoritative frozen file hashes are in `../results/BASELINE.md`.

# B18 — Audit history (architectural)

Record each successful task mutation (`create`, `complete`, `delete`, `archive`,
`append-note`, `add-dependency`) once with monotonic sequence number, UTC
timestamp, actor ID, operation name and task ID. `list-audit` returns entries
in sequence order. Rejected operations add no entry; task mutation and its
entry succeed or fail together. Migrating existing storage starts an empty
history; user creation is not a task mutation.

common_requirement_context.benchmark/baseline.md:
# External baseline contract (before B01)

The interface is a subprocess CLI run from an isolated working directory.
Commands print exactly one JSON value to stdout on success (exit 0); expected
application failures print `{"error":"CODE"}` to stderr (exit 1). Commands
persist across separate processes in `tasks.json` in that directory. `list`
on missing storage returns `[]` without creating the file.

Each task result has exactly `id`, `title`, `description`, `status`, `priority`,
`created_at`, and `due_date`. IDs are unique nonempty strings; timestamps are
UTC ISO strings ending in `Z`. Lists sort by `(created_at, id)` ascending.

* `create --title T --description D [--priority LOW|NORMAL|HIGH]
  [--due-date UTC_TIMESTAMP]`: nonblank title, verbatim description, new ID,
  status `pending`, priority default `NORMAL`, current creation timestamp,
  due date default `null`. Blank title fails `invalid_title`; malformed or
  non-UTC due date fails `invalid_due_date` without changing storage.
* `list`: return all tasks including completed tasks.
* `list-high`: return only HIGH tasks (including completed ones).
* `list-overdue`: return only pending tasks with a non-null due date **strictly
  earlier** than current UTC time. Undated and completed tasks are excluded.
* `complete --id ID`: pending task becomes completed and is persisted; a
  missing ID fails `task_not_found`, an already completed task fails
  `invalid_transition`, both without altering the stored file.
* `delete --id ID`: remove and return the task (pending or completed); missing
  ID fails `task_not_found` without altering storage.
* `migrate`: explicit conversion of legacy unversioned records to version 3
  (add `priority: NORMAL`, `due_date: null`) and version 2 records to version 3
  (add `due_date: null`); return `{"migrated": N}`. Running on current data or
  absent storage returns `{"migrated": 0}`. Legacy reads fail
  `migration_required` without changing data. New writes use a version-3
  envelope with `schema_version` and `records`.

Malformed JSON and invalid record shape, duplicate IDs, blank IDs/titles,
invalid enums and timestamps fail `invalid_state` on read. Failed operations
must not mutate persisted bytes. An exact-time overdue boundary can be checked
only with a controlled clock; the external CLI oracle checks widely separated
past and future instants instead of relying on timing-sensitive sleeps.

The oracle exercises *both* executable CLIs with fresh subprocesses and
independent temporary directories; it asserts this contract before comparing
normalized outcomes. Random IDs and wall-clock timestamps are checked for
properties, not falsely required to be byte-identical across tracks.
common_requirement_context.benchmark/requirements/README.md:
# Frozen sequential change set

Execute B01–B20 in numeric order; a change is cumulative. Each file states an
observable API and acceptance criteria, not an implementation strategy. New
fields on existing tasks require an explicit `migrate` path; ordinary reads of
old storage must report `migration_required` without mutation. Migration is
atomic, returns the number of migrated tasks, and is idempotent. Missing IDs
return `task_not_found` unless a request explicitly defines another error.
Successful operations output JSON; application errors use the baseline JSON
error envelope and exit 1. New list commands use the baseline `(created_at,
id)` sort unless stated otherwise. Existing commands remain compatible unless
a request expressly changes them. Errors must leave observable state intact.

IDs and test cases are fixed before execution; correcting a faulty requirement
requires a recorded protocol deviation, never a silent retroactive edit.
The authoritative frozen file hashes are in `../results/BASELINE.md`.

obligations.source_quote:
# B19 — Daily recurring tasks (architectural)

Allow creation with `--recurrence-days N`, a positive integer, only when a due
date is provided. Omitted recurrence is null; migrated tasks receive null.
Invalid interval or missing due date fails `invalid_recurrence`. Successfully
completing a recurring task also creates exactly one new pending task with a
fresh ID, same title, description, priority, tags, source, category, owner,
notes and project assignment (when applicable), empty dependencies, a new
creation timestamp, and due date equal to the completed task's due date plus
N UTC calendar days. The successor retains recurrence-days N and is not
created again if completion fails. Completion and successor creation are atomic.
The audit history gains two entries in order: `complete` for the original and
`create` for the successor, both attributed to the completing actor.

common_requirement_context.benchmark/baseline.md:
# External baseline contract (before B01)

The interface is a subprocess CLI run from an isolated working directory.
Commands print exactly one JSON value to stdout on success (exit 0); expected
application failures print `{"error":"CODE"}` to stderr (exit 1). Commands
persist across separate processes in `tasks.json` in that directory. `list`
on missing storage returns `[]` without creating the file.

Each task result has exactly `id`, `title`, `description`, `status`, `priority`,
`created_at`, and `due_date`. IDs are unique nonempty strings; timestamps are
UTC ISO strings ending in `Z`. Lists sort by `(created_at, id)` ascending.

* `create --title T --description D [--priority LOW|NORMAL|HIGH]
  [--due-date UTC_TIMESTAMP]`: nonblank title, verbatim description, new ID,
  status `pending`, priority default `NORMAL`, current creation timestamp,
  due date default `null`. Blank title fails `invalid_title`; malformed or
  non-UTC due date fails `invalid_due_date` without changing storage.
* `list`: return all tasks including completed tasks.
* `list-high`: return only HIGH tasks (including completed ones).
* `list-overdue`: return only pending tasks with a non-null due date **strictly
  earlier** than current UTC time. Undated and completed tasks are excluded.
* `complete --id ID`: pending task becomes completed and is persisted; a
  missing ID fails `task_not_found`, an already completed task fails
  `invalid_transition`, both without altering the stored file.
* `delete --id ID`: remove and return the task (pending or completed); missing
  ID fails `task_not_found` without altering storage.
* `migrate`: explicit conversion of legacy unversioned records to version 3
  (add `priority: NORMAL`, `due_date: null`) and version 2 records to version 3
  (add `due_date: null`); return `{"migrated": N}`. Running on current data or
  absent storage returns `{"migrated": 0}`. Legacy reads fail
  `migration_required` without changing data. New writes use a version-3
  envelope with `schema_version` and `records`.

Malformed JSON and invalid record shape, duplicate IDs, blank IDs/titles,
invalid enums and timestamps fail `invalid_state` on read. Failed operations
must not mutate persisted bytes. An exact-time overdue boundary can be checked
only with a controlled clock; the external CLI oracle checks widely separated
past and future instants instead of relying on timing-sensitive sleeps.

The oracle exercises *both* executable CLIs with fresh subprocesses and
independent temporary directories; it asserts this contract before comparing
normalized outcomes. Random IDs and wall-clock timestamps are checked for
properties, not falsely required to be byte-identical across tracks.
common_requirement_context.benchmark/requirements/README.md:
# Frozen sequential change set

Execute B01–B20 in numeric order; a change is cumulative. Each file states an
observable API and acceptance criteria, not an implementation strategy. New
fields on existing tasks require an explicit `migrate` path; ordinary reads of
old storage must report `migration_required` without mutation. Migration is
atomic, returns the number of migrated tasks, and is idempotent. Missing IDs
return `task_not_found` unless a request explicitly defines another error.
Successful operations output JSON; application errors use the baseline JSON
error envelope and exit 1. New list commands use the baseline `(created_at,
id)` sort unless stated otherwise. Existing commands remain compatible unless
a request expressly changes them. Errors must leave observable state intact.

IDs and test cases are fixed before execution; correcting a faulty requirement
requires a recorded protocol deviation, never a silent retroactive edit.
The authoritative frozen file hashes are in `../results/BASELINE.md`.

obligations.source_quote:
# B20 — Projects and permission boundaries (architectural)

Projects are JSON objects with `id`, `owner`, and `members`. They have a unique
nonblank case-sensitive ID, an existing owner user ID, and a set of existing
member user IDs including the owner. `create-project
--id ID --owner USER_ID --actor ACTOR` is allowed to that owner or an ADMIN;
duplicates fail `project_exists`; invalid owner fails `invalid_owner`.
`add-project-member --project ID --user
USER_ID --actor ACTOR` is allowed to the project owner or ADMIN and is
idempotent and returns the updated project. `list-projects` returns projects ordered by ID, including members
ordered by ID. Tasks gain optional `project` (empty string means none);
creation may use `--project ID` only for an existing project. Migrated tasks
are unassigned. `list-project --project ID` returns its nonarchived tasks in
normal order. For a project task, a USER may mutate it only if they own the
task **and** are a project member, or if they own the project; ADMIN may
mutate any task. For creation into a project, the actor must be ADMIN, project
owner, or project member and must satisfy B17 ownership rules. Forbidden
operations fail `permission_denied`; unknown project fails `project_not_found`.

items.meaning: create-project, add-project-member, list-projects, create --project, list-project; task mutations

spans.quote:
# B20 — Projects and permission boundaries (architectural)

Projects are JSON objects with `id`, `owner`, and `members`. They have a unique
nonblank case-sensitive ID, an existing owner user ID, and a set of existing
member user IDs including the owner. `create-project
--id ID --owner USER_ID --actor ACTOR` is allowed to that owner or an ADMIN;
duplicates fail `project_exists`; invalid owner fails `invalid_owner`.
`add-project-member --project ID --user
USER_ID --actor ACTOR` is allowed to the project owner or ADMIN and is
idempotent and returns the updated project. `list-projects` returns projects ordered by ID, including members
ordered by ID. Tasks gain optional `project` (empty string means none);
creation may use `--project ID` only for an existing project. Migrated tasks
are unassigned. `list-project --project ID` returns its nonarchived tasks in
normal order. For a project task, a USER may mutate it only if they own the
task **and** are a project member, or if they own the project; ADMIN may
mutate any task. For creation into a project, the actor must be ADMIN, project
owner, or project member and must satisfy B17 ownership rules. Forbidden
operations fail `permission_denied`; unknown project fails `project_not_found`.
